record_identity.title: Hermes agent ran unattended during intrusion into Thailand’s Ministry of Finance

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Hermes AI-assisted Thailand Ministry of Finance intrusion
incident_identity.date_basis: Hunt.io archived the relevant attack infrastructure from 9–13 July 2026 and published its investigation on 23 July 2026.

summary: Hunt.io and researcher Bob Diachenko reported recovering live attack infrastructure and Hermes agent logs from an intrusion targeting Thailand's Ministry of Finance. The operator configured Hermes in unattended or 'YOLO' mode, bypassing approval prompts, while the agent enumerated ministry systems, assessed privilege-escalation paths and searched files and personnel-record directories. Hunt.io reported evidence of compromise across multiple ministry systems but did not establish the initial-access method or exfiltration of the enumerated office files.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Hunt.io reports 585 files and 470 MB of attack tooling and stolen credentials across exposed directories, active session material, deployed webshells and internal-network evidence. Recovered Hermes logs show autonomous post-compromise enumeration and privilege-escalation assessment. The operator intentionally enabled unattended execution. The recovered archive also contains staged exploits and implants. Their presence does not prove that every tool executed or that listed mitigations were implemented. Logged document searches do not establish file exfiltration. The investigator reports notifying Thailand’s CERT and NCSA on 15 July and receiving acknowledgement that day. Receipt does not establish remediation or final disposition.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: This is a real-world deployment of an autonomous agent as offensive cyber tooling. Because a hostile operator deliberately disabled approval prompts and supplied the attack objective, the occurrence does not by itself establish an internal governance failure of Hermes; the material governance issue is the availability and operationalisation of unattended agentic capability in a live government intrusion. The hostile operator selected unattended mode; this is distinct from an applicable approval control failing to activate. Initial access and exfiltration remain unproved, and no named runtime governance undertaking is established. The human-approval checkpoint and safe-functioning outcomes are Not aligned for this deployment. The remaining stop, monitoring and outbound-policy assessments are Boundary where their operative records are unavailable. Hunt.io’s recovered artefacts include stolen credentials and active session material in the ministry intrusion. These identify authentication objects outside authorised custody. Document-search commands do not independently establish document exfiltration, and the unknown initial-access route is not invented.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows that open-source agents can be configured for unattended offensive operations against a live target. Effective governance therefore depends on target authorisation, tool and execution boundaries, misuse resistance, monitoring and whether an operator can disable approval controls that would otherwise constrain the agent.
assessment_boundaries: The initial-access pathway is not established.
Hunt.io did not establish exfiltration of the office and personnel files enumerated by Hermes.
The public evidence does not identify the underlying foundation-model runtime used by Hermes in this operation.
The operator deliberately enabled YOLO mode, so malicious use is not automatically classified as a Hermes governance failure.

external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: The deliberately unattended agent workflow and sensitive live intrusion actions directly identify human-approval checkpoint design.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The recovered logs show the agent supporting a live government intrusion, including enumeration and privilege-escalation assessment. This offensive deployment created security risks for the targeted ministry. The result covers the reported post-compromise actions. Initial access and exfiltration of the enumerated files remain unproved.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The authenticator-protection proposition requires secret authenticator content to be protected against unauthorised disclosure and modification. The observed secret disclosure/acquisition or custody-changing modification was unauthorised. Hunt.io recovered stolen credentials and active session material in the campaign’s exposed directories. The recovered authentication objects were outside the ministry’s authorised holders. This is a bounded retrospective comparison with the selected control proposition, not a claim of certification or an independently binding historical duty.
